To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel approach for modeling the energy consumption of heterogeneous systems, based on the computation oriented energy modeling of software components.

We present a coarse graining approach that predicts the energy consumption for a given software configuration and a given scheduling policy and we support it by the design and the implementation of a profiling software tool.

we have developed a coarse grained energy model for heterogeneous parallel embedded systems that can be used to estimate the energy consumption of different software components executed according to a specific scheduling policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: 1) the definition of a computational oriented energy modeling approach for heterogeneous embedded systems; 2) the design of a profiling tool to support the approach and 3) the validation of the approach through the implementation of the tool and a set of experiments.
a new methodology and a new approach to model and predict the energy consumption of embedded systems.

the design of a tool for energy modeling of heterogeneous parallel embedded systems, which allows the designer to evaluate and select the most appropriate configuration of the system to be deployed in the field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed modeling approach can be used to predict the energy consumption for a specific set of computational units and can be used to support energy aware planning and optimizations for heterogeneous systems.

our approach can be used to predict the energy consumption of complex embedded systems, composed of heterogeneous computational units, with different software configurations, and with different execution scheduling policies.

the proposed approach can be used for power prediction of a set of computational units, and for energy aware planning of complex systems, by providing the right amount of energy for a set of software configurations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our model can predict energy consumption for a given software configuration, and can be used to optimize energy usage for heterogeneous systems, such as drones, by finding the best software configuration for a specific mission, and by finding the right level of autonomy for the mission.
we propose a novel approach to predict the energy consumption for heterogeneous parallel embedded systems, which we have implemented and tested in a real case scenario.
we provide a novel approach to model the energy consumption of complex heterogeneous systems and present a profiling tool that abstracts and models computational energy behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a coarse grained model can be used to describe energy consumption of heterogeneous systems.
the proposed approach can be used to support the design of a complex embedded system by providing a simple, yet powerful, energy model.

, in order to support the energy aware design of a heterogeneous system, the energy consumption of each component must be described as a function of the software configuration and the scheduling policy.
